purpose: A former Spanish teacher assessing real, previously unseen student work, with his judgement recorded BEFORE the app was run on it.
rater: Kyle Yeh, former high-school Spanish teacher
method: Compositions are genuine College Board AP Spanish Language email-reply responses. The rater had not seen the app's output for them, and was not told their official AP scores before judging. His judgement below was written down before the app was run.
assignment: Email reply (interpersonal writing, 15 minutes). Read a formal email and write a reply in a formal register. The reply must address the questions asked in the message, request additional information by asking a question, and include an appropriate greeting and closing.

what_to_work_on: Grammar — subjunctive, e.g. 'pueden' where the subjunctive is required
Content — be more specific about how the art activity would actually work

comparison.direction: app placed one sublevel BELOW the teacher
comparison.note: The teacher said Intermediate Mid. The official AP score for this composition is 3, and ACTFL's own published comparison associates a 3 with Intermediate Mid -- so the teacher matched the published expectation exactly, and the app sat one sublevel low, the same direction and roughly the same size as the -1.5 bias measured independently on 18 AP samples and on the six-item calibration set.
comparison.diagnosis_agreement: The app identified the same thing the teacher did, and in more detail. The teacher's own priorities were grammar (subjunctive), concordancia, and content specificity.

teacher_verdict.quote: I would definitely use this as a preliminary starting point, and I would even let my students play with it, telling it to trust its error spotting but defer to a conference with me for tailored coaching. The sample exercises are super targeted toward the gaps the student pointed out.
teacher_verdict.named_strength: Can point out specific errors really quickly, in more elaborate detail than the teacher produced by hand.
teacher_verdict.named_limit: Not a substitute for a coaching conference; the teacher would use it as a first pass, not as the final word.
